body.x: Way to Make will participate in the world’s largest technology exhibition CES 2020 opening in Las Vegas on Jan. 7-10 to showcase its portable photocatalysys air purifier LUMO.

In recent years, the demand for air purifiers is increasing due to the issue of fine dust. Not managing the air in your home, school, office, and even your car can have a negative impact on your health. In particular, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as formaldehyde that are emitted from indoor interior materials and oil mist emitted during fueling may cause vomiting, dizziness, and nervous system diseases such as new car syndrome.

In addition, since harmful particles such as VOCs are 1/500 times smaller than PM0.1 (nanofine dust), the photocatalytic technology that completely decomposes the effect is more effective. Transparent substrate coating technology developed by Way to Make uses titanium dioxide photocatalytic nanoparticles to coat transparent substrates with inorganic materials to generate a large amount of electron-hole pairs that are effective for absorbing and decomposing light.
In general, photocatalysts convert harmful substances into water and carbon dioxide when they receive light, and VOCs, odor gases, and viruses are known to be removed in about ten minutes.

LUMO uses energy-efficient UV-A LEDs to produce photocatalytic reactions, and does not generate secondary pollutants such as ozone and radon, and excludes the use of mercury lamps to protect the environment.

In addition, LUMO air purifier is equipped with an ultra-small precision gas sensor so that the LED color changes according to the indoor air quality so that the users can check the air quality in real time. In case of camping and portable use, lithium ion battery can be provided as an option to supply power.

The world’s largest IT show CES shows the trend of the global consumer electronics industry at a glance. It is hosted by Consumer Technology Association (CTA) and is held every January.
